title: Integration discovery - Lattice Ops
next_steps: Send hosted vs dedicated pricing + example throughput SLAs
Share security pack (SOC2, ISO docs) and network diagram for Private deployment
Schedule a 2-hour POC scoping session with infra and SEs next Wed
Provide short LangChain/LlamaIndex sample using Redwood SDKs
action_items: Alex: Email pricing + SLA sheet by 2026-03-29
Maya: Create LangChain + LlamaIndex quickstart repo example by 2026-04-02
Samir: Share internal infra constraints and firewall egress rules by 2026-03-30
header: 2026-03-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE) — Jordan (CTO), Priya (Eng Mgr), Samir (Infra), Leah (SRE)
summary: Intro discovery focused on integration paths (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex support), gateway/proxy setup for private tenancy, rate limiting/quotas and observability hooks. Lattice Ops is leaning towards Dedicated for predictable latency but wants clarity on SDK ergonomics and a short POC to validate batching and KV cache behavior.
transcript:
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we really appreciate you taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood AE, this is Maya our SE. Quick intros?
00:08 Jordan: Jordan here, CTO at Lattice Ops. We run the inference stack for our customer-facing AI features.
00:12 Priya: Priya, engineering manager, mostly interested in integration work and how it affects our dev velocity.
00:16 Maya: Great. Quick agenda, we'll cover SDK options, LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations, network model (gateway/proxy), rate limits and quotas, then observability hooks, and wrap with next steps.
01:02 Jordan: Quick context — we currently call OpenAI for many features but are exploring alternatives for cost and latency. We also have compliance constraints; some workloads must stay in our VPC.
01:20 Alex: Totally. One note up front, we support Hosted, Dedicated and Private — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput; Private can be VPC or on-prem.
01:35 Priya: Curious about dev ergonomics — do you have official SDKs in Python/Node? And adapters for LangChain or LlamaIndex?
01:45 Maya: Yes — official SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. We also maintain example adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex; they're not magical but they're fairly plug-and-play. We'll show a quick snippet.
02:10 Maya: (screen share) Here's a Python example for LangChain: from redwood import RedwoodLLM; chain = LLMChain(llm=RedwoodLLM(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))) — you can swap it into an existing chain with minimal changes. There are small differences in streaming and tool-calling that we document.
03:05 Priya: Nice. Any caveats with LlamaIndex? We use a hybrid of LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented generation.
03:12 Maya: LlamaIndex is supported; we have example connectors and a note about persistent KV caches. For large RAG flows you'll want to tune max_input_tokens and KV cache size — on Dedicated we can expose cache controls so you get better hit rates.
04:00 Samir: On network side, our infra blocks outbound calls except through a corporate gateway/proxy. How does Redwood work with that?
04:12 Alex: Two options: Hosted can be called via your egress gateway (you'd need to allow Redwood IPs or use a proxy), or Private gives you a customer-managed deployment within your VPC where traffic never leaves the network. Dedicated can be fronted by your proxy as well but it's still hosted in Redwood's infra.
04:45 Leah: For Private, what's the auth flow? We need SSO + KMS integration and audit logs.
04:52 Maya: Private supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. We also stream audit logs to your SIEM; retention depends on the plan but we can configure longer retention for compliance.
05:22 Jordan: How about latency? Our SLAs are strict for certain customer flows — can you hit p99 < 150ms for short completions?
05:34 Maya: Short answer: depends on model and token length. For small models on Dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels we often hit p95/p99 in the 80-160ms ballpark for 32–64 token outputs. We'll need to run benchmarks with your prompt set.
06:10 Priya: And cost differences — is batching automatic? We want to balance latency vs unit cost.
06:20 Alex: We have smart batching that adapts by latency SLO; Dedicated gives you more predictable batch sizing because capacity is reserved. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization profiles to hit your cost targets.
06:50 Jordan: Rate limits and quotas — admin team wants per-team quotas and token caps, plus ability to throttle particular routes. Can you do that?
07:05 Maya: Yes, we support per-API-key quotas, per-route throttles, and per-customer rate limiting policies. On Dedicated/Private you can enforce tenant-level policies and integrate with your identity providers for RBAC.
07:38 Priya: Observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and traces linked to our request IDs so our SREs can root-cause.
07:48 Maya: Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns plus tracing hooks where you can inject your request ID header. We also have per-model dashboards and can export traces to Datadog/Tempo/Lightstep.
08:20 Jordan: If we go Dedicated, what's the onboarding time? We have a Q2 deadline for a POC.
08:28 Alex: Typical Dedicated onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on region and capacity reservation. Private can be longer if on-prem. For a POC we usually do a short dedicated burst or Hosted pilot to validate integration in 1–2 weeks.
09:05 Samir: Firewall wise, if Hosted, we need to open egress to your IP ranges — can you provide a published list?
09:12 Alex: Yes, we'll share the CIDR list. Also we support proxy auth if that's easier.
09:30 Priya: About SDK features: is streaming response compatible with LangChain tools and function calling? We rely on function-style tool calls a lot.
09:42 Maya: Streaming and function/tool calling are supported. Small caveat: streaming token-level events differ slightly across languages — we have examples and a test harness.
10:15 Jordan: Any surprises like model variants or quantization affecting output quality? We worry about regression in evaluations.
10:24 Maya: We provide model variant docs and Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles; we also support evaluation hooks so you can run prompt/eval sets and get regression alerts.
11:02 Priya: Great, what's the POC success criteria we should agree on?
11:10 Jordan: For us: 1) integration completes without major SDK changes, 2) p99 latency under 200ms for target prompts, 3) acceptable cost delta vs OpenAI (<30% increase) or improved latency, 4) security checklist items validated (SSO, KMS, egress).
11:30 Alex: Sounds good. We'll draft a POC plan. Proposed next: we send pricing and security docs, Maya will drop LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and we schedule a 2-hour scoping session.
11:48 Priya: One more — observability exports: can we get raw token cost logs for internal chargeback?
11:55 Maya: Yes, raw logs are exportable and we can add fields you need for chargeback.
12:20 Jordan: Competitors — we evaluated Anthropic and some self-hosting pilots. OpenAI for most current usage. The main differentiator will be pricing predictability and private deployment options.
12:50 Alex: Understood. One note — if you want to test KV cache behavior we can run a small benchmark to show hit-rate improvements and cost savings.
13:12 Samir: We'll pull together a list of representative prompts + sample dataset for benchmarking.
13:30 Alex: Perfect. Anything else from anyone?
13:36 Leah: Can you also share an example network diagram for Private deployment?
13:40 Maya: Yep, we'll include that in the security pack.
13:48 Jordan: Thanks, appreciate it.
13:55 Alex: Thanks all, we’ll follow up with the docs and proposed POC plan.
14:02 (call ends)
